## 1. Business Problem

Customer acquisition is costly, and long-term business growth depends on retaining existing customers. Telecom companies often face high churn rates, especially among short-tenure and month-to-month customers.

**Objective:**

* Understand key factors driving customer churn
* Identify high-risk customer segments
* Build a predictive model to estimate churn probability
* Provide actionable retention strategies

---

## 2. Dataset Overview

* **Source:** Telco Customer Churn Dataset (Kaggle)
* **Observations:** Customers of a telecom service
* **Target Variable:** `Churn` (Yes / No)
* **Feature Types:**

  * Demographic
  * Account information
  * Service usage
  * Billing details

library(dplyr)

raw_data <- read.csv("data/telco_churn.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
str(raw_data)

---

## 3. Data Cleaning & Preprocessing

### Steps Performed

* Converted `TotalCharges` from character to numeric
* Removed missing values
* Converted churn variable into binary format (0/1)

**Why:**

* Models require numeric consistency
* Missing values can bias analysis and break models
* Logistic regression requires a binary target

data <- raw_data

data$TotalCharges <- as.numeric(data$TotalCharges)
data <- na.omit(data)

data$Churn <- ifelse(data$Churn == "Yes", 1, 0)

write.csv(data, "data/cleaned_churn_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

---

## 4. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

### Churn Distribution

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(Churn))) +
geom_bar() +
labs(title = "Customer Churn Distribution", x = "Churn", y = "Count")

**Insight:**

* Churned customers form a significant portion of the dataset, justifying deeper analysis.

---

### Churn by Contract Type

ggplot(data, aes(x = Contract, fill = factor(Churn))) +
geom_bar(position = "fill") +
labs(title = "Churn Rate by Contract Type", y = "Proportion")

**Insight:**

* Month-to-month contracts show the highest churn
* Long-term contracts improve retention

---

## 5. Feature Engineering

### Tenure Grouping

Created customer tenure buckets to better interpret lifecycle risk.

data$tenure_group <- cut(
data$tenure,
breaks = c(0, 12, 24, 48, 72),
labels = c("0–1 Year", "1–2 Years", "2–4 Years", "4–6 Years")
)

write.csv(data, "data/final_churn_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

**Why:**

* Improves interpretability
* Helps target retention strategies by lifecycle stage

---

## 6. Statistical Analysis

### Contract Type vs Churn (Chi-Square Test)

chisq.test(table(data$Contract, data$Churn))

**Conclusion:**

* Contract type and churn are statistically dependent

---

## 7. Predictive Modeling (Logistic Regression)

### Model Building

model <- glm(
Churn ~ tenure + MonthlyCharges + Contract,
data = data,
family = "binomial"
)

summary(model)

**Why Logistic Regression:**

* Binary outcome
* Interpretable coefficients
* Widely accepted in business analytics

---

## 8. Model Evaluation

pred_prob <- predict(model, type = "response")
pred <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

accuracy <- mean(pred == data$Churn)
accuracy

**Result:**

* Model accuracy ~ **80%**

---

## 9. Key Insights

* Customers on month-to-month contracts are most likely to churn
* Short-tenure customers show higher churn risk
* Higher monthly charges correlate with churn

---

## 10. Business Recommendations

* Encourage long-term contracts with incentives
* Strengthen onboarding and engagement during the first year
* Proactively monitor high-billing customers

---

## 11. Conclusion

This project demonstrates a complete data analytics workflow in R — from raw data to actionable business insights. The analysis supports strategic decision-making and highlights how predictive modeling can enhance customer retention efforts.
